issues.description: Farm.animals collection type is inconsistent across the problem statement and the reference solution: the task text (Part 3) requires storing unique animals using a Set implemented as a HashSet (no duplicates), but the solution declares `private List<Animal> animals` and initializes it with `new ArrayList<>()`, which allows duplicates and contradicts the uniqueness requirement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make requirements and solution consistent: either (a) change the solution to `private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>();` and update getter/setter/addAnimal accordingly (and ensure Animal defines equality if needed), or (b) change the problem statement to require a List and remove the uniqueness/HashSet requirement.

issues.description: The problem statement contradicts itself about Farm.animals: the UML diagram declares `animals: List<Animal>`, but the Part 3 text requires using a `Set` backed by `HashSet` to enforce uniqueness. This makes it unclear to students which collection type they are expected to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align UML and text: change the UML attribute to `animals: Set<Animal>` (recommended, to match the uniqueness requirement) or update the text to specify `List<Animal>` and clarify whether duplicates/order are allowed.
